messages.author: ec32e5a92a275a89
messages.subject: Mentor's summit
parts:
Until today I had not realized that the Mentor's summit was funded. I'm officially
retired, and my time is spent mostly on community work (see some of the CRAN optimization
stuff -- several packages and parts this year). I am willing to attend the Mentor's Summit
as one of the R group, but am fairly new to this game, so if there are two others eager,
I'll step back so there doesn't have to be a vote or such.

From Carol Smith's emails, I'd guess we have to make up our minds in the next few days.

Cheers,

John Nash

messages.author: 3c04c342136fe2e7
messages.subject: Re: Mentor's summit
parts:
To follow-up on John's post re the mentor summit:

i) It's an 'unconference' as pioneered by the of the O'Reilly Events. It's
semi-structured.

ii) It's a decent way to meet some other folks from other open source projects.

iii) It's always late in October and always at Google HQ which throws in a
spanner for those teaching in Europe.

iv) The crowd is a tad younger on average than John but he would not be the
only gray beard there.

v) I've gone twice; I may go again but I am happy to take a backseat if two
other folks want to go. I sort-of have an invite from someone at Google
to also talk RProtoBuf / Rcpp once there so it may make sense to go.

vi) I guess we have five potential candidates for the two slots in the five
mentors Roger, Stefan, John, Hadley and myself. Stefan just took
himself out of contention, John has raised his had, I hereby do so
tentatively. Roger, Hadley: please ping back.

vii) Admining is an issue. I am waiting on past year's info from Manuel/Fritz
but should get that sorted out.

Cheers, Dirk

--
Dirk Eddelbuettel | e...@debian.org | http://dirk.eddelbuettel.com
